title: Multilayer Authorization & Audit Orchestration Guide for Inference Pipelines
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
This guide defines a unified approach to authorization decisions, audit event capture, regional residency controls, secure SDLC gates, incident response hooks, and compliance-artifact packaging for Redwood Inference’s multilayered model-serving stacks. It is intended for engineers, SREs, security reviewers, and compliance owners responsible for production inference (hosted, dedicated, private).

Purpose and goals
- Reduce gaps between who can take action (RBAC) and what gets recorded (audit logging).
- Ensure evidence required for regulatory review can be assembled within defined SLAs.
- Maintain data residency guarantees while preserving forensics and rollback options.

Scope
Applies to: inference-proxy, routing-bridge, model-orchestrator, kvcache-service, audit-collector, evidence-orchestrator, console-api.
Excludes: developer-local sandboxes, ephemeral test clusters (see dev exception section).

Principles
1) Single truth for entitlement: enforce primary authorization checks at the service edge (inference-proxy) and replicate decisions to downstream services via signed decision-tokens.
2) Immutable audit stream: events are appended in chronological order to the audit-collector; any enrichment is recorded as a new event referencing the original event id.
3) Residency-first packaging: evidence bundles must be created in-region if the request was processed in a geo-fenced deployment.
4) Forensic reproducibility: every rollout and model change should include deterministic artifacts (model SHA, quantization profile id, compilation artifacts).

Ownership and escalation
- Policy authorship: product-security@redwood (primary).
- Operational enforcement: eng-sre (primary for collectors and retention).
- Evidence packaging and audit queries: compliance-team (evidence owner).
- Escalation path: pager -> oncall-security -> engineering owner -> compliance lead.

Glossary (short)
- Decision Token: signed assertion produced by inference-proxy containing principal, role, action, resource, region, and expiry.
- Evidence Bundle: a signed archive containing audit events, artifacts, and a manifest suitable for regulatory review.
- Residency Marker: per-request metadata indicating the controlling region/zone.

High-level architecture (text diagram)
- Client -> inference-proxy (authz check + decision-token) -> routing-bridge -> model-orchestrator -> kvcache-service
- All services -> audit-collector (ingest, enrich, store to immutable lake + hot index)
- evidence-orchestrator queries audit-collector + storage to assemble evidence bundles

RBAC model and role mappings
- Roles: viewer, operator, deployer, svc_account, compliance_auditor, infra_admin.
- Resource types: model, deployment, dataset, audit-log, billing, key-material.
- Minimal privileges: prefer role composition instead of coarse admin access.

Example role-to-action table (use in policy reviews)
| Role | Allowed actions (examples) | Typical owner | Notes |
| viewer | read:model, read:deployment-status | product | read-only; no token minting |
| operator | invoke:model, tail-logs | eng-sre | cannot rotate keys |
| deployer | create:deployment, promote:canary | eng-platform | gated behind SDLC gates |
| compliance_auditor | query:audit-logs, create:evidence-bundle | compliance | cannot change artifacts |

Decision-token lifecycle
1. inference-proxy authenticates principal (OIDC or mTLS).
2. Evaluate policies (policy-engine), produce signed Decision Token (JWT with nested claim digest).
3. Downstream services verify signature and cache ephemeral mapping for 5 minutes.
4. Decision Tokens are logged (token id + hash) to audit-collector; token payload not stored raw unless for compliance request.

Audit schema and retention (summary)
- Core event fields: event_id, timestamp_utc, principal_id, role, action, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, region, decision_token_id, outcome, metadata_hash, parent_event_id.
- Enrichment fields (when present): stack_trace_id, artifact_shas, model_sha, compile_profile_id.
- Ingestion SLA: 99.9% of events must be indexed in the hot index within 5 minutes of generation.

Retention policy (table)
| Artifact | Hot index retention | Immutable archive retention | Rationale |
| audit-hot-index | 90 days | - | fast query for triage |
| audit-immutable | - | 7 years (default) | regulatory/legal |
| model-binaries | - | 3 years or as per customer contract | reproducing inference |
| evidence-bundles | - | 7 years or per customer | packaged for audits |
| ephemeral-dev-logs | 7 days | 30 days | minimal retention for devs |

Data residency controls
- Residency Marker must be attached at request acceptance.
- If residency == EU, evidence-orchestrator will spawn assembly job in eu-region storage and sign bundle using regional KMS key.
- Cross-region transfer requires documented customer consent and a cross-region-transfer ticket.

Secure SDLC gates (integrations)
- Feature branches that touch model-serving runtime require: unit tests, performance regression check, cryptographic signing of build artifact, and a security checklist pass.
- Deployment gating steps: (1) ci/build artifact SHA published; (2) sign-off from owner; (3) canary with audit-sampling enabled; (4) ramp policy.
- Checklist (minimum): dependency scanning, secret-scan, signed provenance, RBAC review for new roles, audit schema changes reviewed.

Incident response integration and evidence capture (step-by-step)
1) Triage: Incident commander tags incident with scope and residency.
2) Freeze: If scope includes cross-customer access, raise restricted-access and snapshot relevant audit streams (IDs).
3) Collection: evidence-orchestrator run: fetch events (by request_id and time window), pull model artifacts, collect decision-token logs, assemble manifest.
4) Preservation: Store Evidence Bundle to an immutable store (region-bound). Record bundle_id in incident timeline.
5) Short-term playback: compliance-team may request sanitized playback in a dev-safe environment (no customer PII).
6) Handoff: Provide bundle_id and signed manifest to legal or external auditors under escrow.

Evidence bundle manifest example (text)
- bundle_id: BNDL-2026-000123
- principal_scope: service-account:orchestrator-42
- time_window: 2026-01-15T10:12:00Z - 2026-01-15T10:20:00Z
- artifacts: [model_sha:abc123, compile_profile:qp-6, token_hash:...]
- retention_class: 7y
- residency: eu-west-1
- signer: regional-kms:projects/redwood/keys/eu-signing-key

Operational runbooks (short)
- Adding a new role:
  1. Proposal PR with justification and least-privilege mapping.
  2. SDLC security checklist and reviewer assignment.
  3. Deploy policy in canary with audit-sampling at 100%.
  4. After 7 days without escalation, promote to global.

- Responding to missing audit events:
  1. Verify producer service connectivity to audit-collector (health check).
  2. Query temporary ingress buffer for request_id.
  3. If buffer unavailable, run reconstruction job from storage snapshots.
  4. If reconstruction fails, escalate to eng-sre + security and open evidence-restoration ticket.

Query examples and tooling
- Example Kibana/LogQL quick checks: (text)
  - Find events for request: query: request_id: "r-1234" | sort timestamp_utc desc
  - Timeline for principal: principal_id: "svc:orchestrator-42" and timestamp_utc >= "2026-02-01"
- evidence-orchestrator CLI (example)
  - redwood evidence assemble --request-id r-1234 --start 2026-02-01T12:00Z --end 2026-02-01T12:10Z --out bundle-BNDL-123.tar.gz

Compliance checklist for audits
- Produce evidence-bundle signed by regional KMS.
- Provide manifest with event hashes and chain-of-custody log.
- Demonstrate SDLC gating artifacts (build provenance, policy PRs).
- Show retention-policy enforcement and immutable archive checksums.

Privacy and PII handling
- PII must be redacted in any non-secure evidence playback. Evidence bundles should include a PII-summary file that lists redaction points and justification.
- Access to raw PII-bearing bundles requires legal approval and restricted confidentiality classification.

Exceptions and temporary access (short summary)
- Developer exceptions: limited to dev clusters and must be approved by eng-sre for a maximum of 48 hours.
- Emergency cross-region transfer: requires emergency-approval workflow with 2 approvers (security + compliance) and automatic timebound revocation.

Validation and rollout plan
- Stage rollout: dev -> staging (30 days) -> prod-canary (7 days) -> prod.
- Acceptance tests: synthetic traffic that asserts Decision Token verification failure cases, audit latency checks, residency-label correctness, and evidence assembly completes within 15 minutes for nominal windows.
